name: Volite / Volift

card.summary: Juvéderm Volite is a low-concentration hyaluronic acid gel injected into the skin for smoothness and hydration; trial data exist but are mostly single-arm and manufacturer-linked.
card.note: Volift is a separate product name; the skin-quality gel is Volite. Evidence is mostly single-arm or manufacturer-linked.

quick.overview:
Juvéderm Volite (also marketed as Skinvive, with the gel called VYC-12) is a crosslinked hyaluronic acid gel placed in the skin rather than beneath it, aiming to improve smoothness, hydration and fine texture rather than add volume. Volift is a different product in the same Juvéderm family, a filler used for lines and folds.
It is discussed in aesthetic circles as a 'skin booster' that can be paired with botulinum toxin or fillers. Published studies include a prospective single-arm study, a retrospective cohort and a small randomised split-face trial.
quick.mechanism: Clinicians describe injecting small amounts of gel into the dermis at several points, where the hyaluronic acid binds water and is intended to improve surface smoothness and hydration. Volite is described as a lower-concentration, longer-lasting gel than older boosters.
quick.risks: Reported effects are mainly injection-site reactions such as swelling, redness and bruising. Hyaluronic acid fillers carry rarer risks including lumps, delayed inflammatory reactions and vascular complications. It is a clinician-administered, regulated device.

lead: Juvéderm Volite is a crosslinked hyaluronic acid (HA) gel (VYC-12, marketed in the US as Skinvive) injected into the skin, rather than under it, to improve skin quality attributes such as surface smoothness and hydration.[1][11] People seek it for a smoother, more hydrated and more luminous complexion rather than for added volume, and it is described as providing longer-lasting effects at a lower HA concentration than traditional fillers.[2][11]

In a prospective single-arm study, patients with moderate or severe cheek skin roughness received VYC-12 and the authors reported it as safe and effective for improving facial skin topography.[1] In the US, the FDA approved Skinvive on 15 May 2023 for improving cheek skin smoothness in adults over 21, on the basis of a randomized, evaluator-blinded pivotal study reported by the manufacturer.[11] Other published work includes a Brazilian retrospective cohort,[2] a randomised split-face trial combined with botulinum toxin,[3] and several registered manufacturer-sponsored trials.[4][5][6]

Volift is a separate Juvéderm product in the same Vycross family, a higher-concentration gel used for lines and folds such as the nasolabial folds and perioral region, not for skin hydration.[12][13] The two names are covered together here because they are often confused.

SKINVIVE by Juvéderm, 15 May 2023 (cheek skin smoothness, adults over 21) [11]

paras: Hyaluronic acid fillers are generally crosslinked to prolong their duration.[7] Wikipedia describes Juvéderm as a hyaluronic-acid-based line approved by the FDA in 2006 for nasolabial folds and used for lips, hollows and scars, with correction usually absorbed over six to nine months.[14] Volite is positioned as a skin-quality product intended to improve texture and hydration instead of volume.[1][2]

The manufacturer describes Skinvive as an intradermal microdroplet injection of HA gel with a small amount of lidocaine, indicated for the cheeks, with an optional touch-up a month after the first session and a required provider training program before purchase.[11]

A 2015 plastic surgery review of the Vycross technology, which mixes high- and low-molecular-weight HA with enhanced crosslinking, lists Voluma at 20 mg/mL (high G prime, for vertical lift and volume), Volbella at 15 mg/mL (lower G prime, for lips and fine lines) and Volift at 17.5 mg/mL, between the two, giving subtle lift with some spread and a use in the perioral region and in fine lines.[12]

A randomized, double-blind split-face study in 48 women compared DKL23 with Juvéderm Volift for moderate-to-severe nasolabial folds. Both gels produced significant improvement on the Wrinkle Severity Rating Scale at each timepoint to nine months, with similar changes between them.[13] An Italian experience with two Vycross fillers in the perioral and lip regions has also been reported.[15] This is a different use from Volite, which targets skin quality.

The prospective single-arm VYC-12 study enrolled subjects with moderate or severe cheek skin roughness on the Allergan Skin Roughness Scale, who were treated in the cheeks and forehead and/or neck, with touch-up at 30 days and optional repeat treatment at 9 months. Of 131 subjects, 31 (23.7 percent) received touch-up. The responder rate (cheeks with at least a 1-point improvement) was 96.2 percent at month 1, 76.3 percent at month 4, 34.9 percent at month 6 and 87.1 percent after repeat treatment. Instrument-measured skin hydration improved significantly from baseline at all timepoints through month 9, and treatment-related adverse events were mild or moderate.[1]

A retrospective cohort of patients treated between 2018 and 2019 at a private clinic in Rio de Janeiro examined routine-practice use and safety.[2] A prospective study of 45 patients combined Fraxel laser, microbotox and a very low G prime HA (Volite) and reported that 98 percent showed smoother, more hydrated skin, though the combination design does not isolate the gel.[16]

The manufacturer's pivotal study for US approval was randomized, multicenter and evaluator-blinded. The company reported that 58 percent (73 of 125) of treated patients had at least a 1-point improvement on the Allergan Cheek Smoothness Scale at one month and 56 percent (69 of 124) at six months, and that patient-reported satisfaction with radiance, hydration, refreshed appearance and skin health was higher at six months than before treatment.[11]

A randomised, double-blind split-face trial in 25 women combined onabotulinumtoxinA with Volite (Skinvive) for periorbital wrinkles and assessed efficacy and durability with electromyography, the Merz scale and FACE-Q at up to six months.[3]

Registered trials include a healthy-volunteer study of skin quality attributes,[9] studies in China for neck lines (n=159) and perioral lines (n=198),[4][5] a phase 2/3 skin quality study,[6] and a phase 4 study of combined facial treatment and subject satisfaction.[17] Their outcomes have not been published.

Hyaluronic acid fillers can cause bruising, redness, pain, swelling, lumps, and rarely vascular occlusion or granulomatous reactions.[7] A 2026 computational study modelled risk of delayed immune and fibrotic reactions across 26 fillers and genotypes; it is a modelling analysis rather than a clinical trial.[10]

The manufacturer lists common reactions as redness, lumps, swelling, bruising, tenderness, pain, firmness, discoloration and itching, most mild or moderate. Its key warning is unintended injection into a blood vessel, which can cause serious and possibly permanent complications including vision changes, blindness and stroke. Contraindications include a history of multiple severe allergies or anaphylaxis and allergy to lidocaine or Gram-positive bacterial proteins, and the label advises limiting strenuous exercise, sun and heat exposure, and alcohol for 24 hours. Safety in other body areas has not been established.[11] Wikipedia notes Allergan's advice against use in patients with severe allergies and the risk of granulomas with Juvéderm products.[14]

timeline.event: Juvéderm HA filler receives FDA approval.[14]
Prospective study of VYC-12 for facial skin topography published.[1]
Retrospective cohort of Juvéderm Volite use in Brazil published.[2]
Randomised split-face trial combining botulinum toxin and Skinvive published.[3]
FDA approves Skinvive by Juvéderm for cheek skin smoothness.[11]

Smoother, more radiant-looking cheeks and skin surface
angle.text: Volite is injected by a clinician into the skin of the cheeks and sometimes the neck or forehead to improve smoothness and hydration, with results the manufacturer reports lasting about six months. Volift, a firmer gel, is used for fine lines and folds.
